Hi Emily —

Great questions — short answers up front, then the checklist below.

- We support both AWS PrivateLink and VPC peering for Private VPC deployments.
  - PrivateLink: easier to avoid routing changes in customer VPCs and useful when you want to expose a service endpoint; recommended if you don’t want cross-account route tables.
  - VPC peering: lower per-request overhead and may be simpler if you already run peering across accounts; requires route table updates.
- IP allowlist: we can provide stable egress ranges for management/control plane and a set of endpoints for application traffic. Sample CIDRs (examples only): 34.200.140.0/24, 34.200.141.0/24. Recommend allowlisting these for initial review; final ranges will be provided in the SOW.
- mTLS: We support mutual TLS for management endpoints as an optional control (we can provision certs or integrate with your KMS).

Attached: redwood_vpc_checklist.pdf — includes required security artifacts, port lists, suggested subnets, and a short ops runbook. Also adding links to our docs and the HubSpot deal: 
- Tech doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/abc123
- HubSpot deal: HS-000342

Proposed next steps
1) Can we schedule a 30-min technical sync next week? Vivek (cc’d) from our infra team can run through peering/PrivateLink options and confirm routing/firewall specifics.
2) After the tech sync, I’ll share the formal networking appendix and sample SOW for procurement review.
3) If you prefer, we can initiate a non-production proof-of-concept in a dedicated test VPC to validate connectivity before signing.

Please let me know two 30-min windows that work for Sam and the procurement contact and we’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa Cole
